## Overview

This project examines the mean-variance portfolio optimization problem.

The objective is to identify portfolio weights that provide an appropriate
balance between expected return and risk.

## Mathematical Formulation

Let

$$
w =
\begin{bmatrix}
w_1 \\
w_2 \\
\vdots \\
w_n
\end{bmatrix}
$$

represent the vector of portfolio weights.

The expected portfolio return is

$$
\mathbb{E}[R_p] = w^\top \mu,
$$

where $\mu$ is the vector of expected asset returns.

Portfolio variance is

$$
\sigma_p^2 = w^\top \Sigma w,
$$

where $\Sigma$ is the covariance matrix.

A minimum-variance portfolio can be obtained by solving

$$
\begin{aligned}
\min_w \quad & w^\top \Sigma w \\
\text{subject to} \quad
& \mathbf{1}^\top w = 1.
\end{aligned}
$$

## Python Implementation

```{python}
#| echo: true
#| warning: false

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

expected_returns = np.array([0.08, 0.10, 0.12])

covariance_matrix = np.array([
    [0.040, 0.006, 0.008],
    [0.006, 0.090, 0.010],
    [0.008, 0.010, 0.160]
])

weights = np.array([0.50, 0.30, 0.20])

portfolio_return = weights @ expected_returns
portfolio_variance = weights @ covariance_matrix @ weights
portfolio_volatility = np.sqrt(portfolio_variance)

results = pd.DataFrame({
    "Metric": [
        "Expected return",
        "Variance",
        "Volatility"
    ],
    "Value": [
        portfolio_return,
        portfolio_variance,
        portfolio_volatility
    ]
})

results
```

## Interpretation

The model combines expected returns, asset variances and correlations
to estimate the risk-return characteristics of a portfolio.

## Limitations

- Expected returns are difficult to estimate.
- The covariance matrix may change over time.
- Transaction costs are not included.
- The model assumes that variance is an appropriate measure of risk.
